episode_title: How to Make Your Engineering Team More Creative | Steven Puri, Ex-DreamWorks and Fox Executive

real_qa.q: How do you foster creativity in technical teams like engineers and software developers?
real_qa.r: The most creative people in both technical and creative fields have very similar processes. Creativity is the art of being nimble with your brain, allowing new things to pass through you and become manifest in the world. It applies to creating code, designs, and words—any act of bringing forth something that might not have existed before. Leaders must create a space where anyone can challenge anyone's ideas without fear, because safety is essential for creativity to flourish.
real_qa.requete: how to make engineering teams more creative

real_qa.q: What role does psychological safety play in encouraging pattern-breaking creativity?
real_qa.r: At the top tier of creatives, there is a truly creative environment where ideas are not proprietary but evaluated on what's best for the project. The middle layer is where people get possessive and proprietary, which stifles creativity because team members are afraid to speak up. You have to show the room as a leader that challenging ideas is a good thing, then return to the question: 'What's best for the project?' This allows people to contribute without fear of being beaten up for their ideas.

real_qa.q: Why did the Godzilla film fail after Independence Day's success?
real_qa.r: After Independence Day made $800 million and became the third highest-grossing movie in film history at the time, the filmmakers were treated as creative geniuses and the culture of challenging every idea disappeared. No one felt comfortable bringing up fundamental problems in the Godzilla script, and they practically shot the second draft without iteration. The loss of that challenge process was a failure—the movie flopped because no one felt safe questioning the creative direction.
real_qa.requete: why did Godzilla movie flop after Independence Day

real_qa.q: How do flow states and deep thinking enable breakthrough creativity?
real_qa.r: Flow states are highly concentrated states where you become one with the work and distractions fall away. You don't look at the clock and can do your best work. If you want to break the pattern, you have to go deeply into it, which doesn't happen in five-minute increments. Leaders should allow people to block their calendars for at least an hour daily for unstructured time, trusting them to think deeply about how to move the company forward—this is where breakthrough ideas emerge.

real_qa.q: How do LLMs and artificial intelligence differ from true human creativity?
real_qa.r: LLMs study all human output and predict the next word based on probability—they extend the pattern of the past into now, which is what most screenwriters and engineers do through reversion to the mean. The interesting part of human creativity is breaking the pattern: going deep and doing what LLMs do not do, which is pushing back the frontier. True creativity is not trying to be like an LLM and just repeat patterns—it's understanding what the pattern holds while breaking it.
